strengths.I002-v2: Faster de-risking (three sessions at up to 6% each, so up to 18 points a week) combined with a drawdown cushion, plus a hand-arithmetic worst-case estimate for 2008, 2020 and 2022 and a new stress-prior mechanism that steers ERC away from co-crashing assets.
strengths.I003-v2: Very simple and precisely specified. Daily 3.5% slew limit with a stated 1.5% drift margin, and an explicit droop law that cuts exposure to 10% at 15% drawdown, so the trading gates hold by construction.

verdicts.reason: I002 pairs a faster exposure cut with a reasoned worst-case loss estimate for correlated sell-offs, whereas I003's 3.5%/day slew takes about 3-4 weeks to de-risk and offers no worst-case argument.

strengths.I008-v2: Weekday sleeves are a natural staggering mechanism that guarantees a trade every day. Risk is budgeted equally across three classes by rule, and there are three de-risking layers: trend gate, vol cap and drawdown brake.
strengths.I004-v2: The N-1 style reserve sizes exposure from a stress-floored, simulated loss, which is the most explicit drawdown argument. It also has asymmetric ramps that cut risk twice as fast as they restore it.

verdicts.reason: I008's sleeves and 19.5% weekly stop make both constraints hold with margin, while I004's 4%x5=20% cap leaves no room for drift or the minimum swap and so risks breaching the turnover gate.

strengths.I008-v2: Stress-day covariance blended with the full sample, a trend gate, a vol cap and a drawdown brake that goes to a 25% floor by 11% DD. Class risk budgets are fixed by rule and the operational spec is highly precise.
strengths.I003-v2: Minimal parameters, an equal-risk bucket structure, a 10% permanent cash reserve, and explicit turnover headroom (17.5% plus drift) with daily trading.

verdicts.reason: I008 layers a trend gate, vol cap and drawdown brake with sleeves that can cut quickly, whereas I003 relies on a single slow slew-limited droop that a 2020-style gap would outrun.

strengths.I002-v2: Explicit turnover margin (weekly traded <=18% plus a 2% drift margin) from three capped sessions, a novel PC1 stress prior, and a cushion-based bound with worked scenario estimates.
strengths.I004-v2: Stress-floored reserve multiplier acts like a measured CPPI, with asymmetric 4%/2% ramps and a plan to log exceedance against the reserve S.

verdicts.reason: I002 leaves an explicit drift margin under the 20% cap, whereas I004's 4%/day cap sums to exactly 20% before drift and the minimum swap, so its turnover gate is not secured by construction.

strengths.I003-v2: Few parameters, simple to code, and a stated turnover budget with drift margin. Equal-bucket risk structure and an all-time-peak backstop at 15% DD.
strengths.I004-v2: The most principled drawdown sizing, from a stress-floored reserve, and cluster-level ERC with a trend-to-cash filter.

verdicts.reason: I003 has few, principled parameters and a real turnover margin, while I004 stacks many tuned floors and thresholds (0.17, 0.5, 2.33, 1260d, 504d, half-worst-loss) and can breach the 20% cap once drift is counted.

strengths.I002-v2: Rank-1 PC1 stress prior on ERC covariance is a new mechanism, and it is backed by a hand-worked worst-case estimate and a smooth exposure throttle with 3 capped sessions per week.
strengths.I008-v2: Risk is budgeted equally across growth, duration and real classes by rule (growth capped at 1/3 of risk), so no class dominates risk at any date, and the layered trend/vol/drawdown de-risking is explicit.

verdicts.reason: I008 enforces class-level risk budgets by rule, while I002's ERC across 10 assets lets the five equity-like ETFs carry about half the risk with no class cap, and its throttle is admittedly mild.
